title: When sorting primitive values (integers, bools, chars, as well as arrays, slices, and tuples of such items), it is typically better to use an unstable sort than a stable sort.
summary: Typically, using a stable sort consumes more memory and cpu cycles. Because values which compare equal are identical, preserving their relative order (the guarantee that a stable sort provides) means nothing, while the extra costs still apply. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Finds items imported through std when available through alloc.
summary: Crates which have no_std compatibility and require alloc may wish to ensure types are imported from alloc to ensure disabling std does not cause the crate to fail to compile. This lint is also useful for crates migrating to become no_std compatible. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Finds items imported through std when available through core.
summary: Crates which have no_std compatibility may wish to ensure types are imported from core to ensure disabling std does not cause the crate to fail to compile. This lint is also useful for crates migrating to become no_std compatible. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usages of str.trim().split("\n") and str.trim().split("\r\n").
summary: Hard-coding the line endings makes the code less compatible. str.lines should be used instead. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: This lint checks for .to_string() method calls on values of type &str.
summary: The to_string method is also used on other types to convert them to a string. When called on a &str it turns the &str into the owned variant String, which can be more specifically expressed with .to_owned(). Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for all instances of x + _ where x is of type String, but only if string_add_assign does not match.
summary: This particular Add implementation is asymmetric (the other operand need not be String, but x does), while addition as mathematically defined is symmetric, and the String::push_str(_) function is a perfectly good replacement. Therefore, some dislike it and wish not to have it in their code. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for string appends of the form x = x + y (without let!).
summary: It’s not really bad, but some people think that the .push_str(_) method is more readable. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the use of .extend(s.chars()) where s is a &str or String.
summary: .push_str(s) is clearer Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Check if the string is transformed to byte array and cast back to string.
summary: It’s unnecessary, the string can be used directly. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for the as_bytes method called on string literals that contain only ASCII characters.
summary: Byte string literals (e.g., b"foo") can be used instead. They are shorter but less discoverable than as_bytes(). Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for <string_lit>.chars().any(|i| i == c).
summary: It’s significantly slower than using a pattern instead, like matches!(c, '\\' | '.' | '+'). Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for slice operations on strings
summary: UTF-8 characters span multiple bytes, and it is easy to inadvertently confuse character counts and string indices. This may lead to panics, and should warrant some test cases containing wide UTF-8 characters. This lint is most useful in code that should avoid panics at all costs. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Nothing.
summary: This lint has been deprecated Clippy puts this lint in the deprecated group, at the level none.

title: Checks for usage of libc::strlen on a CString or CStr value, and suggest calling count_bytes() instead.
summary: libc::strlen is an unsafe function, which we don’t need to call if all we want to know is the length of the c-string. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for excessive use of bools in structs.
summary: Excessive bools in a struct is often a sign that the type is being used to represent a state machine, which is much better implemented as an enum. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Detects struct fields that are prefixed or suffixed by the same characters or the name of the struct itself.
summary: Information common to all struct fields is better represented in the struct name. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.
